sentence: This project offers imaging services and advice to researchers who study obesity and nutrition in humans.
This project builds a mathematical model of how the kidney proximal tubule takes up proteins, including effects of sex and fluid flow.
This project studies the structure and function of immune molecules found in sharks to learn about the matching molecules in humans.
This project designs versions of a virus used in gene therapy that escape antibodies and studies how antibodies block the virus.
This project develops metal complexes that could be used as probes to image the chemistry of the body noninvasively.
This project studies the social and structural causes of cancer and develops programs and policies that aim to reduce its burden.
This project studies how glaucoma-linked genes in the mitochondria, the energy-producing parts of cells, affect disease in patients.
This project studies how a protein complex controls a fusion protein found in low-grade gliomas in children.
This project uses mass spectrometry to study the role of proteins in cancer and to find cancer biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
This project studies how specialized dendritic cells shape the germinal center, where antibodies improve, in response to vaccines.
This project builds a monitoring device and app that helps track hemophilia and reduce the risk of unexpected bleeding.
This project follows existing participants in rural communities with high environmental exposures, collecting samples and exposure surveys linked to breast cancer.
This project studies how an abnormal protein found in brains with Alzheimer's disease changes, clumps together and gets cleared.
This project studies how poxviruses disrupt a metabolic sensor protein in host cells to avoid the innate responses to infection.
This project tests whether blocking lipid production in pancreatic cancer cells makes radiation therapy and chemotherapy work better.
This project studies how losing a vulnerable type of neuron affects hippocampus memory in Alzheimer's disease and tests a way to stimulate those neurons.
This project uses large language models to pull information about cancer variants from scientific literature and make it available to researchers and clinicians.
This project studies whether stress signaling caused by radiation drives changes in cells that lead to esophageal cancer.
This project works to improve polygenic scores so they predict coronary artery disease risk better across populations and are more useful in the clinical setting.
This project studies what factors lead to clonal hematopoiesis and why outcomes differ by race, to find people at higher risk.
